newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe urged to push ahead with reforms.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe urged to push ahead with reforms.

text.p: Zimbabwe needs to push ahead with economic reforms and build on its achievements if it is to win more foreign investment needed to speed up growth, Anglo American chief executive in Zimbabwe said on Wednesday.

Phillip Baum told a Confederation of Zimbabwe Industries (CZI) congress that the country needed to raise its investment levels to 28 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) annually from 17 percent to sustain economic growth of six percent a year and create sufficient jobs to cut down on high unemployment.

"The gap between the existing annual level of Z$12 billion (U.S.$1.05 billion) of investment and the required Z$20 billion (U.S.$1.76 billion) is a daunting Z$8.0 billion (U.S.$703 million) per year," he said.

"If domestic savings were increased to a heroic 20 percent (from 14 percent per year), the gap of Z$3.6 billion (U.S.$316 million), or eight percent, would have to be provided by the injection of foreign capital," he said.
In Zimbabwe's 17 years of independence, it had only attracted one significant foreign investment -- the U.S.$200 million Australian-owned Hartley Platinum Mine Project, he said.
